ownership: Root proposed the intersected residual inference. bounded_idea_supply checked the proof, one-sided counterexamples, finite closure and prior limits without native payloads or new counts. The mathematical principle is not claimed as globally novel.
premises: C is a fixed freely uniquely decodable set of nonempty words over a fixed working-unit alphabet. Let M=C*. The complete original word strings W are contained in M. This means uniqueness of codeword factorization for ALL finite C-concatenations, not just for a selected natural-language grammar. No prefix or suffix freedom and no bound on |C| are assumed.
lemma: If x,xy,yz,z all belong to M, then y belongs to M.
proof: Choose C-parses A of x, B of xy, D of yz and E of z. Then the concatenated codeword lists A followed by D and B followed by E both spell the same visible word xyz.
Free unique decodability forces these two lists to be identical. Both A and B are therefore prefixes of that same codeword list.
Because codewords are nonempty and |xy|>=|x|, B cannot be a strictly shorter list prefix than A. Hence B=A followed by a codeword list F (empty only if y is empty).
Cancelling the visible prefix x from spell(B)=xy=spell(A)spell(F) gives spell(F)=y. Thus y is in C*. This proves the inference without requiring either one-sided quotient rule.

finite_rule.initial_set: S begins with the finite original complete word set W. Derived strings are obligations in C*, not new attested manuscript words.
finite_rule.suffix_residuals: R(S)={y nonempty: there exists nonempty x with x and xy in S}.
finite_rule.prefix_residuals: L(S)={y nonempty: there exists nonempty z with yz and z in S}.
finite_rule.update: Add every member of R(S) intersection L(S), retaining one explicit pair of witnesses from each side. Repeat until no new string is added.
finite_rule.soundness: Induction on additions uses the lemma: every premise is already certified in C*, so each inferred center is also in C*.
finite_rule.finiteness: Every new center is a proper nonempty suffix and prefix of already present strings, hence a contiguous working-unit substring of an original word. The finite union of original-word substrings bounds the universe; no unbounded concatenation enumeration is needed.
finite_rule.certificate: For each addition y store four earlier node IDs witnessing x,xy,yz,z. Check exact tuple equalities xy=x+y and yz=y+z, nonempty operands and strict earlier indices. This makes the proof DAG acyclic. Do not infer y from a witness which depends on that same not-yet-certified y.
finite_rule.scope: A fixed point is closure under this stated finite inference system. It is not automatically the complete free hull, a complete characterization of every freelyUDcover, or proof that an unforced unit can be omitted by some UDtable.

If all active alphabet singletons were forced, any additional longer codeword would collide with its singleton factorization. Only the singleton identity table could then be freelyUD. This is a general conditional theorem, NOT an unknown outcome on the present full W because of the explicit countermodels below.

That expansion implication has no prefix/suffix/cardinality premise beyond the proved singleton obligations and freeUD. It still requires fixed non-erasing literal expansion, exact whole-group/source-word correspondence and the retained working-unit reading. Contextual meanings, null expansions or changed groups are outside it.
